problems.label: 1b
problems.prompt: A disk of radius 2 rolls to the right at unit speed; $P$ starts 1 unit above the center. Which vector-parametric equation gives $\overrightarrow{OP}(t)$?
problems.solution: Center: $(t,2)$. Rolling without slipping gives $t = 2\theta$, so $\theta = t/2$ clockwise from vertical. Add the radius vector from the center to $P$: $(-\sin(t/2), -\cos(t/2))$. So $\overrightarrow{OP}(t) = (t - \sin(t/2),\; 2 - \cos(t/2))$.

problems.label: 1c
problems.prompt: Describe the shape of the curve $C$ traced by $P$ (compare with your sketch and the mathlet trace).
problems.solution: An elongated periodic wave — a curtate trochoid. $P$ sits inside the rim, so the curve has no cusps and never touches the x-axis: it dips to height $1$ and rises to height $3$ while the center moves steadily right.

problems.label: 2b
problems.prompt: Which parametrization gives the unit circle centered at the origin in the plane $x + 2y + z = 0$?
problems.solution: Use $r = u\cos t + v\sin t$ with unit, orthogonal $u, v$ that are both $\perp n = (1,2,1)$. Take $u = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}(1,-1,1)$ and $v = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(-1,0,1)$, parallel to $u_1 \times n$ with $u_1 = (1,-1,1)$.

problems.label: 3a
problems.prompt: Which equations describe all lines through the origin that lie in the plane $x + 2y + z = 0$?
problems.solution: A direction vector $(a,b,c)$ must satisfy $a + 2b + c = 0$, so $c = -a - 2b$. With the separate case $b = 0$ (the line $x = t,\,y = 0,\,z = -t$), dividing by $b$ gives the one-parameter family $x = \alpha t,\; y = t,\; z = -(\alpha + 2)t$ with $\alpha = a/b$.

problems.label: 3b
problems.prompt: Give a geometric description of this family of lines, and explain why one parameter suffices.
problems.solution: The lines through $O$ whose direction vectors lie in $P$ — i.e. all lines through $O$ contained in $P$. Unit direction vectors of such lines trace the unit circle in $P$, a 1-dimensional set; that matches the single parameter $\alpha = a/b$.

problems.label: 4b
problems.prompt: Light at $(0,0,4)$ projects the curve $(\cos t, \sin t, 2)$ onto the tilted plane $my + z = 0$. Derive $r_\alpha(t)$, the vector-parametric equation of the shadow.
problems.solution: The ray from $(0,0,4)$ through $(\cos t, \sin t, 2)$ is $(0,0,4) + u(\cos t, \sin t, -2)$. Substituting into $my + z = 0$ gives $mu\sin t + 4 - 2u = 0$, so $u = \frac{4}{2 - m\sin t}$. Therefore $r_\alpha(t) = \frac{4\cos t}{2-m\sin t}\,i + \frac{4\sin t}{2-m\sin t}\,j - \frac{4m\sin t}{2-m\sin t}\,k$.

problems.label: 4c
problems.prompt: Comparing $r_\alpha(t)$ with the enlarged circle $r_0(t) = (2\cos t,\, 2\sin t,\, 0)$, at which corner point $t$ is the distortion largest (for small $\alpha > 0$)?
problems.solution: The difference satisfies $|r_\alpha - r_0| = \frac{2\sqrt{5}\,m\,|\sin t|}{|2 - m\sin t|}$. At $t = 0, \pi$ this is $0$; at $t = \pi/2$ it is $\frac{2\sqrt{5}\,m}{2-m}$; at $t = 3\pi/2$, $\frac{2\sqrt{5}\,m}{2+m}$. The largest is at $t = \pi/2$.
